parsed.main_gap: The crucial lemma that every term’s primes at most A form a good set is wholly unproved; it is the central arithmetic step needed to deduce periodicity.

errors.description: The claimed induction provides neither an induction hypothesis nor an argument showing that deleting prime factors greater than A preserves intersection with every sequence term. This is not a standard or routine detail, and all subsequent periodicity depends on it.
errors.quote: **Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). \(\square\)

errors.description: The later reference to a construction \(Rp^k\) does not repair the omission: neither \(R,p,k\) nor the construction’s properties are defined or proved anywhere in the solution.
errors.quote: The construction \(Rp^k\) repairs this boundary issue while preserving exactly the small-prime support; the lemma proves the strengthened hypothesis.

parsed.notes: Sections 1 and 3 give a valid characterization and a correct deduction of the desired identity conditional on the lemma. However, the omitted lemma is the substantive heart of the problem, so the proof is far from complete.
